GUIDANCE ANALYSIS: Deere & Company — Q1 2026

METRIC: Equipment operations net sales growth
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: mid-single-digit net sales growth
UNIT: % year-over-year
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Equipment operations net sales, reported basis
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management believes fiscal 2026 marks the bottom of the current cycle.
- Growth in Small Agriculture & Turf and Construction & Forestry is expected to more than offset lower Production & Precision Agriculture sales.

METRIC: Consolidated net sales
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Company net sales versus fiscal 2025
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Net sales are expected to increase, with the anticipated Production & Precision Agriculture decline more than offset by improvements in Construction & Forestry and Small Agriculture & Turf.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture net sales
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Down 5% to 10%
UNIT: % year-over-year
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture segment net sales, reported-currency basis
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- North American large-agriculture sales are expected to remain subdued and South America is expected to soften.
- Stabilization in North American large-agriculture fundamentals, an improving used-equipment market, and increased replacement demand provide partial support.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture price realization
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Roughly 1.5 points of positive price realization
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture segment net-sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects positive full-year price realization in South America despite Q1 discounts and incentives.
- North American pricing has been positive.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture currency translation
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: About 3 points of positive currency translation
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture segment net-sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- A weaker U.S. dollar versus relevant currencies, particularly the euro and Brazilian real, is expected to support reported sales.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture operating margin
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 11% to 13%
UNIT: operating margin
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture segment operating-margin forecast
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Tariffs, unfavorable product and regional mix, and higher warranty expenses are headwinds.
- Improving North American production and a more normal geographic mix later in the year are expected to aid margins.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture operating margin
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Double-digit margins each quarter
UNIT: operating margin
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Each quarter for the remainder of fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Date Range
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture segment quarterly operating-margin outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects geographic mix to normalize as North American production increases through the year.

METRIC: Small Agriculture & Turf net sales
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Up about 15%
UNIT: % year-over-year
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Small Agriculture & Turf segment net sales, reported-currency basis
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Solid dairy and livestock demand, a modest turf-market recovery, stronger order activity, and healthy field inventories support growth.
- Positive price realization and currency translation are included in the outlook.

METRIC: Small Agriculture & Turf price realization
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 2 points of positive price realization
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Small Agriculture & Turf segment net-sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Positive pricing is included in management's segment sales outlook.

METRIC: Small Agriculture & Turf currency translation
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 2 points of positive currency translation
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Small Agriculture & Turf segment net-sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Foreign-currency translation is expected to benefit reported segment sales.

METRIC: Small Agriculture & Turf operating margin
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 13.5% to 15%
UNIT: operating margin
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Small Agriculture & Turf segment operating-margin forecast
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Higher shipment volumes, favorable mix, and price realization support profitability.
- Higher tariffs are a partial offset.

METRIC: Construction & Forestry net sales
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Up around 15%
UNIT: % year-over-year
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Construction & Forestry segment net sales, reported-currency basis
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Construction and compact-construction retail activity and order books have strengthened.
- Infrastructure spending, declining interest rates, rental demand, data-center projects, and roadbuilding demand support the outlook.

METRIC: Construction & Forestry price realization
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: About 2.5 points of positive price realization
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Construction & Forestry segment net-sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects price increases to realize later in the year after a delayed start caused by rapid backlog build.
- The forecast was revised down by 0.5 point versus the prior outlook because of the timing of price realization.

METRIC: Construction & Forestry currency translation

PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Just over 2 points of positive currency translation
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Construction & Forestry segment net-sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Foreign-currency translation is expected to benefit reported segment sales.

TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Construction & Forestry segment operating-margin forecast
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Higher sales volumes and production efficiencies support margins.
- Higher tariffs remain a headwind.

METRIC: Worldwide Financial Services net income attributable to Deere & Company
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Approximately $840 million
UNIT: USD millions
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Worldwide Financial Services net income attributable to Deere & Company
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The outlook increased primarily because of a lower provision for credit losses.
- Favorable financing spreads are supportive, while a lower average portfolio and prior-period special items are unfavorable.

METRIC: Worldwide Financial Services net income

NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Financial Services outlook versus fiscal 2025
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects net income to be down year over year.

TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year

MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:

METRIC: Effective tax rate

UNIT: effective tax rate
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Company effective-tax-rate guidance
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- No additional causal explanation was provided.

METRIC: Cash flow from equipment operations
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: $4.5 billion to $5.5 billion
UNIT: USD billions
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Cash flow from equipment operations

GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative

TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026

BASIS: Equipment-operations operating cash flow versus fiscal 2025

COMPARABLE EARNINGS ANALYSIS: Deere & Company — Q2 2026
STRICT REPORT WINDOW: 2026-04-06 to 2026-05-20

COMPARABLE: CNH Industrial N.V. (CNH)
REPORT DATE: 2026-04-30
REPORTED PERIOD: First quarter 2026, ended 2026-03-31
WHY COMPARABLE: CNH is a direct global agricultural-equipment manufacturer with overlapping exposure to tractor and combine replacement demand, farmer income and input costs, trade policy, dealer-channel inventory, pricing, and precision-agriculture investment. Its Agriculture segment is therefore directly relevant to Deere's Production & Precision Ag business, though geographic mix, product mix, sourcing, and dealer inventories differ.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- North American large-tractor and combine demand
- Farmer commodity-price, input-cost, and trade-policy exposure
- Agricultural-equipment price realization versus unit-volume mix
- Tariff and transportation-cost pressure
- Dealer-channel inventory alignment
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- North American agricultural-equipment retail demand, especially large tractors and combines [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: CNH reported North American industry sales volume down 7% year over year for tractors below 140 HP, down 27% for tractors above 140 HP, and down 6% for combines. CNH Agriculture net sales were $2.596bn, up 1% reported but down 4% at constant currency; favorable price realization and currency offset lower volume. Agriculture adjusted EBIT fell from $139m to $27m, with lower North American and South American volumes cited as primary drivers.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This is a negative directional demand read-through for Deere's Production & Precision Ag, particularly for large equipment. It does not imply Deere will experience CNH's sales or profit change because Deere's order book, production cadence, North American mix, and price realization can differ.
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1567094/000156709426000009/ex991q126.htm
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1567094/000156709426000009/q12026final.htm
- Farm economics: low commodity prices, elevated farm input costs, and uncertain trade conditions [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: CNH said farmers continued to face low commodity prices, high input costs, and an uncertain trade environment. It kept its Agriculture outlook at sales down 5% to flat for 2026 and stated it would maintain low production and continue channel-inventory reduction in response to these conditions.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The conditions are negative for farmers' willingness to fund discretionary equipment replacement and support a cautious demand assumption for Deere. The effect should be moderated rather than copied because Deere has different customer credit, regional, and product exposure.
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1567094/000156709426000009/ex991q126.htm
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1567094/000156709426000009/q12026final.htm
- Tariff and transportation costs [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: CNH cited tariff impacts among the drivers of Agriculture adjusted EBIT declining to $27m from $139m. It also identified rapid changes in tariff and transportation costs as headwinds, while noting favorable price realization only partly offset lower volume and cost pressure.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This is a negative cost/margin read-through to Deere's manufacturing operations, conditional on Deere's country-of-origin sourcing and mitigation actions. It is not assumed to be equal in dollars or margin rate.
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1567094/000156709426000009/ex991q126.htm
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1567094/000156709426000009/ex991q126.htm
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1567094/000156709426000009/q12026final.htm

COMPARABLE: AGCO Corporation (AGCO)
REPORT DATE: 2026-05-05
REPORTED PERIOD: First quarter 2026, ended 2026-03-31
WHY COMPARABLE: AGCO is a direct global producer of tractors, combines, hay equipment, sprayers, and precision-agriculture technology sold through dealer channels. Its high-horsepower equipment and precision-agriculture commentary shares especially close demand and investment exposure with Deere's Production & Precision Ag segment, although AGCO's regional mix is more Europe-weighted.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- North American high-horsepower tractor and combine demand
- Farmer crop economics, input costs, credit, and trade conditions
- Precision-agriculture productivity and return-on-investment spending
- Dealer inventory and production alignment
- Tariff, freight, and input-cost pressure
- Equipment pricing
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Cautious crop-farmer economics and weaker North American large-equipment retail demand [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: AGCO reported North American industry retail tractor sales down 8% and combine sales down 7% year over year in the first three months of 2026, with the most pronounced tractor declines in higher-horsepower categories. It attributed continued pressure to farm economics, grain-export demand, and elevated input costs, and said demand for new equipment remained measured and selective.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This is a negative directional read-through for Deere's large agricultural equipment demand. Deere's realized shipments can differ from industry retail because manufacturer production and dealer inventory movements can temporarily diverge from retail activity.
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/880266/000088026626000054/a2026earningsreleaseq1.htm
  SOURCE: https://news.agcocorp.com/2026-05-05-AGCO-REPORTS-FIRST-QUARTER-RESULTS
- Precision-agriculture and productivity investment [INDUSTRY, POSITIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: AGCO stated that farmers continued to prioritize technology and precision-agriculture investments that provide productivity, efficiency, and return-on-investment benefits, even while broader equipment demand was selective. It reported North American constant-currency sales growth supported by high-horsepower tractors, hay equipment, and sprayers, while characterizing precision agriculture as an area where it outpaced the market.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This partially offsets the weak broad-equipment-demand signal for Deere's Production & Precision Ag business: technology-enabled, productivity-focused purchases may prove more resilient than discretionary iron replacement. The effect is not scaled from AGCO because AGCO specifically cited its own market-share and portfolio execution.
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/880266/000088026626000054/a2026earningsreleaseq1.htm
  SOURCE: https://news.agcocorp.com/2026-05-05-AGCO-REPORTS-FIRST-QUARTER-RESULTS
- Tariff, freight, and other input-cost pressure [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: AGCO reported that adjusted operating-margin improvement was partly offset by higher cost inputs including tariffs. It further said North American operating income was reduced by tariff-related costs and factory under-absorption; its call quantified approximately $25m of incremental tariff cost, concentrated in North America, and approximately $0.20 per share of incremental freight and fuel-related cost pressure in its full-year bridge.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This is a negative margin read-through for Deere, but not a dollar-for-dollar transfer: tariff exposure depends on each manufacturer's sourcing, import classifications, pricing actions, and production footprint. Factory under-absorption is excluded from the read-through because it is partly a company-specific production decision.
  SOURCE: https://news.agcocorp.com/2026-05-05-AGCO-REPORTS-FIRST-QUARTER-RESULTS
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/880266/000088026626000054/a2026earningsreleaseq1.htm
- Pricing discipline amid selective demand [INDUSTRY, POSITIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: AGCO maintained a 2% to 3% full-year pricing expectation and stated that first-quarter pricing was stronger in North America and Europe, while pricing was materially weaker in Latin America. Its outlook assumed positive pricing alongside cost controls, although tariff and freight costs remained headwinds.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The peer evidence supports some ability for agricultural OEMs to defend price in stronger regions, partially cushioning volume and cost pressure at Deere. It should not be treated as proof of the same price realization for Deere, particularly by region and product category.
  SOURCE: https://news.agcocorp.com/2026-05-05-AGCO-REPORTS-FIRST-QUARTER-RESULTS
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/880266/000088026626000054/a2026earningsreleaseq1.htm
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/880266/000088026626000054/a2026earningsreleaseq1.htm
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://news.agcocorp.com/2026-05-05-AGCO-REPORTS-FIRST-QUARTER-RESULTS

PRELIMINARY COMPARABLE-ONLY METRIC ADD-ONS:
- Worldwide net sales and revenues: 0 USDm (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: 0 USDm. The qualifying comparable signal is mixed: CNH's Agriculture sales were down 4% at constant currency as price offset lower volume, while AGCO reported growth but explicitly identified company-specific share gains, Europe recovery from prior dealer destocking, and favorable currency. No Deere sales baseline, regional/product revenue weighting, or independently supportable peer-to-Deere elasticity was supplied, and the instruction prohibits use of target-company news and requires only qualifying comparables in the adjustment. Therefore a dollar scaling would be non-defensible.
  ASSUMPTION: CNH and AGCO are the only qualifying direct public agricultural-OEM comparables identified before 2026-05-21.
  ASSUMPTION: Weak North American large-equipment retail is a negative common signal, while pricing and precision-technology demand provide offsets.
  ASSUMPTION: No target-company historical revenue, consensus baseline, or target sales mix is used for scaling.
  ASSUMPTION: Zero denotes absence of a defensible dollar translation, not an assertion of no underlying demand effect.
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1567094/000156709426000009/ex991q126.htm
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/880266/000088026626000054/a2026earningsreleaseq1.htm
  SOURCE: https://news.agcocorp.com/2026-05-05-AGCO-REPORTS-FIRST-QUARTER-RESULTS
- Diluted EPS (GAAP): 0 USD / share (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: 0 USD / share. A GAAP EPS add-on cannot be mapped defensibly from peer operating commentary without Deere's share count, tax rate, interest/financial-services contribution, and GAAP reconciliation. CNH's reported GAAP EPS decline includes consolidated and financial-services effects; AGCO's reported EPS and guidance bridge include tax-rate, finance-joint-venture, restructuring, and buyback effects that are not shared operating exposures. Those items are excluded under the stated methodology.
  ASSUMPTION: Only shared demand, price, and tariff/freight factors are eligible; peer-specific finance, tax, restructuring, and repurchase effects are excluded.
  ASSUMPTION: No target-company EPS bridge, diluted share count, tax rate, or financing income is used.
  ASSUMPTION: The underlying directional operating read-through is mildly negative from large-equipment demand and tariff/freight costs, partly offset by pricing and precision demand, but it cannot be converted to GAAP EPS per share from qualifying peer evidence alone.
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1567094/000156709426000009/ex991q126.htm
  SOURCE: https://news.agcocorp.com/2026-05-05-AGCO-REPORTS-FIRST-QUARTER-RESULTS
- Production & Precision Ag operating profit: 0 USDm (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: 0 USDm. CNH's Agriculture adjusted EBIT declined by $112m year over year, citing lower volume, tariffs, labor inflation, and higher SG&A/R&D; AGCO's North American operating result also faced tariff costs and under-absorption, while its precision/productivity demand and pricing commentary were supportive. Directly scaling either peer's segment-profit change to Deere would import non-shared cost structures, geographic mix, factory utilization, and accounting definitions. With no permissible Deere operating-profit base or peer-to-target margin-transfer coefficient, zero is the defensible preliminary add-on.
  ASSUMPTION: CNH Agriculture adjusted EBIT is a directional industry indicator, not a GAAP-equivalent transfer metric.
  ASSUMPTION: AGCO's tariff and under-absorption effects demonstrate pressure but are not transferred quantitatively because the latter is partly company-specific.
  ASSUMPTION: Precision-agriculture productivity spending and pricing are treated as partial offsets to weak large-equipment retail.
  ASSUMPTION: No Deere segment-profit baseline, production schedule, cost base, or segment-margin assumption is used.
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1567094/000156709426000009/ex991q126.htm
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/880266/000088026626000054/a2026earningsreleaseq1.htm
  SOURCE: https://news.agcocorp.com/2026-05-05-AGCO-REPORTS-FIRST-QUARTER-RESULTS

events.title: Temporary 10% U.S. import surcharge imposed
events.summary: The White House proclaimed a temporary 10% ad valorem surcharge on most imported articles, effective February 24, 2026. The surcharge is to apply for 150 days and is in addition to applicable duties except where specified.

events.title: Deere declares $1.62-per-share quarterly dividend
events.summary: Deere's board declared a quarterly dividend of $1.62 per share. The dividend is payable May 8, 2026, to shareholders of record on March 31, 2026.
source_headlines: Deere & Company declares quarterly dividend of $1.62 per share

events.title: Administration announces farmer aid and calls for lower tractor prices
events.summary: Reuters reported that the administration was distributing $12 billion in aid to farmers and planned additional loan guarantees. The administration also urged equipment manufacturers, including Deere, to lower prices. The report cited higher fertilizer and diesel costs and continued trade uncertainty for growers.
source_headlines: Trump announces farmer support measures and calls on tractor makers to lower prices

events.title: USDA reports 2026 intended planting mix shift
events.summary: USDA reported that U.S. farmers intended to plant 95.3 million acres of corn in 2026, down 3% year over year, and 84.7 million acres of soybeans, up 4%. All-wheat planted area was forecast to decline 3%.
source_headlines: USDA: farmers intend to plant less corn and more soybeans in 2026

events.title: U.S. revises Section 232 metal-tariff treatment
events.summary: The White House revised tariff treatment for covered steel, aluminum, copper, and derivative articles, effective April 6, 2026. The proclamation provided a 25% rate for certain derivative products, maintained other higher rates, applied duties to the full customs value of covered derivative articles, and modified derivative-product scope.
source_headlines: U.S. modifies Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum, and copper derivative products

events.title: Deere agrees to proposed $99 million right-to-repair settlement
events.summary: Associated Press reported that Deere agreed to place $99 million into a proposed class-action settlement fund for customers who paid Deere or authorized dealers for certain large-agriculture-equipment repairs. Deere denied wrongdoing. The proposed settlement required court approval and included commitments related to repair tools.
source_headlines: Deere agrees to proposed $99 million right-to-repair class-action settlement

events.title: USDA forecasts lower 2026 net farm income and working capital
events.summary: USDA forecast 2026 nominal net farm income of $153.4 billion, down 0.7% from 2025. Nominal net cash farm income was forecast to increase 3.0% to $158.5 billion. Farm-sector working capital was forecast to decrease 9.2%, while debt was forecast to increase 5.2%.
source_headlines: USDA forecasts mixed 2026 farm-income outlook, with lower net farm income but higher cash income

events.title: USDA initial 2026/27 outlook projects higher corn and soybean prices
events.summary: USDA's initial 2026/27 outlook projected U.S. corn prices of $4.40 per bushel, compared with $4.15 for 2025/26, and soybean prices of $11.40 per bushel, compared with $10.40. The outlook projected lower U.S. corn production and exports and higher soybean output, crush, and exports.
source_headlines: USDA's initial 2026/27 crop outlook projects higher corn and soybean farm prices

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Q2 2026 forecast = prior reported Q1 2026 actual $9,611m + $3,651m = $13,262m. Contributions sum: GUIDANCE +3,651; E1-E8 0; COMPARABLES 0.

event_contributions.affected_line: Sales volume, selling price, currency translation and segment mix
event_contributions.transmission_path: FY equipment-operations net-sales growth guidance is first phased into the standalone fiscal Q2 revenue forecast using FY2025 Q2 segment seasonality and Q1 2026 actuals. Segment equipment sales plus Financial Services/other revenue flow directly to worldwide net sales and revenues.
assumptions: Fiscal Q2 is the standalone 13-week period ending near early May; it is not H1.
FY2026 PPA sales use the midpoint of management's -5% to -10% range: -7.5%.
FY2026 SAT and CF sales use management's approximately +15% guidance.
Financial Services and other Q2 revenue are held approximately flat with Q2 2025 because management guided Financial Services on net income rather than revenue.
FY2025 Q2 segment revenue is used as the quarter-specific seasonal base rather than mechanically dividing FY guidance by four.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. FY2025 equipment sales = PPA $17,311m + SAT $10,224m + CF $11,382m = $38,917m. Guided FY2026 equipment sales = ($17,311m × 92.5%) + ($10,224m × 115.0%) + ($11,382m × 115.0%) = $16,013m + $11,758m + $13,089m = $40,860m, or +5.0%, consistent with mid-single-digit equipment growth. Q2 phasing: PPA $5,230m × 92.5% = $4,838m; SAT $2,994m × 115.0% = $3,443m; CF $2,947m × 115.0% = $3,389m; Financial Services plus other revenue held at Q2 2025 $1,592m. Q2 forecast = $4,838m + $3,443m + $3,389m + $1,592m = $13,262m. Change versus Q1 actual = $13,262m - $9,611m = +$3,651m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Production cost and inventory cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: The temporary import surcharge could increase landed component/whole-good cost, but does not directly establish a Q2 shipment or sales-price change. Any broad tariff effect was already contemplated in Deere's stated FY tariff-cost outlook.
assumptions: Management's approximately $1.2bn FY2026 tariff-cost estimate, reiterated after the February 20 action, remains the controlling guidance baseline.
No supportable evidence quantifies a distinct incremental Q2 revenue effect from this temporary surcharge.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental Q2 revenue effect = $0m because the event changes cost exposure, not an evidenced sales-volume or sales-price assumption, and management did not revise sales guidance after the event.

event_contributions.affected_line: Financing cash flow and retained earnings
event_contributions.transmission_path: A declared common dividend reduces cash and retained earnings when declared/paid; it does not affect revenue recognition or operating sales.
assumptions: No dividend-induced change in shipment volume, pricing, or revenue recognition is evidenced.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Revenue effect = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Farmer liquidity, selling price and Financial Services credit
event_contributions.transmission_path: Farmer aid could support affordability and demand, while public calls for lower tractor prices could pressure realization. The offsetting directions cannot be translated into an incremental Q2 shipment or price amount beyond guidance.
assumptions: Government-program support and challenging farm economics were already included in management's FY agriculture outlook.
No Deere price action, funded incentive program, order cancellation, or revised sales outlook was disclosed.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental Q2 revenue effect = $0m: the aid/price-pressure narrative is directionally mixed and already contemplated in guidance; no defensible dollar elasticity is available.

event_contributions.affected_line: Production & Precision Ag sales volume and dealer inventory
event_contributions.transmission_path: A corn/soy acreage mix shift can affect farm cash economics and longer-cycle equipment demand, but it does not establish a near-term Deere shipment change in the fiscal Q2 reporting window.
assumptions: The acreage report does not quantify Deere market share, dealer orders, production changes, or Q2 deliveries.
Management had already cited crop production, available farm acres and farm fundamentals as agricultural-cycle drivers.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental Q2 revenue effect = $0m because no company-specific, quarter-recognizable unit-volume transmission is evidenced.

event_contributions.affected_line: Production cost, inventory cost and possible selling price
event_contributions.transmission_path: The revised Section 232 treatment can alter costs of metals and covered derivative articles; it does not itself create an evidenced Q2 revenue change. Any pricing response would be indirect and was not quantified.
assumptions: Deere's FY guidance already included a dynamic tariff environment, approximately $1.2bn of tariff costs and neutral price-cost inclusive of tariffs.
No post-event revised Deere sales guidance or price-realization guidance was issued before the cutoff.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental Q2 revenue effect = $0m; prevent double counting with GUIDANCE tariff and price-cost assumptions.

event_contributions.affected_line: Selling, administrative and general expense
event_contributions.transmission_path: The proposed repair settlement affects legal/SG&A expense and accrued liabilities rather than sales recognition.
assumptions: No material aftermarket-revenue offset is assumed in Q2.
The settlement does not change Q2 worldwide revenue in this forecast.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Revenue effect = $0m; the identified transmission is expense/accrual, not net sales and revenues.

event_contributions.affected_line: Farm working capital, dealer inventory and Financial Services credit
event_contributions.transmission_path: Lower sector working capital could restrain equipment affordability, while higher net cash farm income partly offsets. The mixed macro effect does not identify an incremental Deere Q2 shipment amount.
assumptions: Management guidance already incorporated challenging row-crop farm fundamentals, government liquidity support and potential elevated receivable write-offs.
No Deere-specific order, dealer-inventory or credit-loss revision was disclosed.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental Q2 revenue effect = $0m because the mixed USDA update cannot be defensibly scaled to Deere shipments beyond guidance.

event_contributions.affected_line: Farmer cash economics and future Production & Precision Ag demand
event_contributions.transmission_path: Higher projected crop prices could improve replacement economics, but the outlook was published after Deere's fiscal Q2 end and principally affects future crop-year decisions rather than recognized Q2 shipments.
assumptions: No retroactive Q2 revenue recognition is assumed from a May 12 commodity-price outlook.
Management guidance already included commodity-price and crop-demand uncertainty.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Q2 revenue effect = $0m because the event occurred after the fiscal Q2 period end and lacks evidence of a recognized Q2 order/shipment effect.

event_contributions.affected_line: Large-agriculture sales volume, price realization and tariff/freight cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: CNH and AGCO indicate weak North American large-equipment retail and cost pressure, offset partly by pricing discipline and precision-technology demand. The signal is qualitative and overlaps Deere's guidance.
assumptions: No peer-to-Deere revenue elasticity, Deere regional sales base, or incremental order data supports a dollar translation.
Comparable-specific share, factory-utilization, financial-services, tax and restructuring effects are excluded.
event_contributions.calculation: Incremental Q2 revenue effect = $0m. The comparable summary's preliminary add-on is zero; applying a peer sales rate would double count Deere's guided weak PPA volume and introduce non-comparable mix effects.

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Q2 2026 GAAP EPS forecast = $5.56/share; prior reported Q1 2026 diluted EPS = $2.42/share; projected change = $5.56 - $2.42 = +$3.14/share. Contributions sum: GUIDANCE +$3.41; E6 -$0.27; E1-E5, E7-E8 and COMPARABLES $0.00.

event_contributions.affected_line: Sales volume, price, currency, production cost, operating expenses, interest and tax
event_contributions.transmission_path: Guided equipment sales growth and segment-margin ranges are phased into Q2 consolidated revenue and pretax income. Consolidated pretax income is taxed at the midpoint of the 25%-27% guided tax range and divided by forecast diluted shares.
assumptions: The Q2 consolidated revenue forecast before discrete events is $13,262m, linked to the requested Worldwide net sales and revenues metric.
A 22.0% pre-discrete consolidated operating-income margin reflects Q2 seasonality and the guided recovery in SAT/CF, while retaining tariff pressure.
Net non-operating expense is $790m, anchored to Q2 2025 interest expense of $784m and consistent with Deere's lower-rate/lower-borrowing Q1 commentary.
Tax rate is the 26.0% midpoint of Deere's FY guidance.
Diluted shares are 270.0m, modestly below Q1's 270.9m because Q1 repurchases reduced shares; no unannounced buyback acceleration is assumed.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Pre-discrete Q2 operating income = $13,262m × 22.0% = $2,917.64m. Pre-discrete pretax income = $2,917.64m - $790m = $2,127.64m. Pre-discrete net income = $2,127.64m × (1 - 26.0%) = $1,574.45m. Pre-discrete diluted EPS = $1,574.45m / 270.0m = $5.83/share. Guidance contribution versus Q1 EPS = $5.83 - $2.42 = +$3.41/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: COGS and inventory cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: Higher import duties would reduce operating income through production costs and then reduce pretax income, net income and EPS. However, Deere retained its tariff outlook after the event, so the effect is included in guidance.
assumptions: No incremental tariff charge beyond management's approximately $1.2bn FY tariff-cost assumption is supportable.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental pretax effect = $0m; EPS effect = $0m × (1 - 26.0%) / 270.0m = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: Financing cash flow and retained earnings
event_contributions.transmission_path: The dividend is a financing/equity distribution rather than an expense in net income; it does not affect diluted EPS except through any future share-count changes, which are not assumed.
assumptions: No repurchase, issuance, or other share-count change caused by the dividend is evidenced.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Net-income effect = $0m; diluted EPS effect = $0m / 270.0m = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: Selling price, sales volume, provision for credit losses
event_contributions.transmission_path: Farmer aid could support demand and credit performance, while calls for lower equipment prices could pressure revenue and margin. Both effects overlap with guidance and cannot be separately quantified.
assumptions: Management already included government liquidity support, weak farm fundamentals, sales incentives and potential receivable write-offs in its outlook.
No Deere-specific price cut, subsidy pass-through, or provision revision was disclosed.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental pretax effect = $0m; EPS effect = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: Sales volume and dealer inventory
event_contributions.transmission_path: Planting-intention changes affect farm economics and future replacement demand but provide no defensible incremental Q2 revenue, cost, provision or tax amount.
assumptions: No Deere order-book, production or dealer-inventory response was quantified.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental pretax effect = $0m; EPS effect = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: COGS, inventory cost and pricing
event_contributions.transmission_path: Modified metal tariff treatment could affect operating cost and potentially pricing, then pretax income and EPS. Deere's unchanged tariff outlook prevents an incremental estimate.
assumptions: No quantification of Deere's affected import base, supplier pass-through or Q2 recognized cost is available.
Avoid double counting tariff exposure embedded in GUIDANCE.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental pretax effect = $0m; EPS effect = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: Selling, administrative and general expense / legal settlement accrual
event_contributions.transmission_path: A specified $99m proposed settlement fund is modeled as a discrete Q2 legal/SG&A expense, reducing consolidated operating income, pretax income, net income and diluted EPS. It does not affect revenue.
assumptions: The announced agreement makes the stated $99m a reasonable central Q2 accrual estimate, subject to court approval.
The amount is treated as incremental to the February 1 unresolved-legal-matters accrual because the supplied information does not establish that this specific settlement was already fully accrued.
Tax deductibility is assumed at the 26.0% guided effective tax rate.
No change in diluted shares is assumed.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Q2 operating-income adjustment = -$99m. After-tax net-income effect = -$99m × (1 - 26.0%) = -$73.26m. EPS effect = -$73.26m / 270.0m = -$0.271/share, rounded to -$0.27/share. Final EPS = ($13,262m × 22.0% - $99m - $790m) × 74.0% / 270.0m = $5.56/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: Sales volume, Financial Services receivables and provision for credit losses
event_contributions.transmission_path: Lower farm working capital is adverse for affordability and credit, while higher cash farm income is supportive. The mixed effect was already directionally reflected in guidance.
assumptions: No company-specific incremental delinquency, receivable-originations or provision forecast was disclosed.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental pretax effect = $0m; EPS effect = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: Future sales volume, customer credit and provision for credit losses
event_contributions.transmission_path: Higher crop-price projections could support future farm profitability, but publication after fiscal Q2 end prevents a supportable Q2 recognized earnings effect.
assumptions: No retroactive Q2 sales, financing or provision impact is assumed.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Incremental pretax effect = $0m; EPS effect = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: Agricultural sales volume, price realization and tariff/freight cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: CNH and AGCO provide a mildly negative operating read-through from large-equipment demand and costs, partly offset by pricing and precision investment. Their results do not provide a defensible Deere GAAP EPS bridge.
assumptions: Peer-specific financial-services, tax, restructuring, share-repurchase and accounting effects are excluded.
Comparable effect is already qualitatively consistent with Deere's PPA guidance; no incremental Deere pretax dollar is supportable.
event_contributions.calculation: Incremental pretax effect = $0m; EPS effect = $0.00/share. No peer earnings figure is mechanically transferred.

earnings_bridge.calculation: Standalone fiscal Q2 consolidated bridge, USDm except per-share data: operating income = revenue × operating margin + discrete other operating income = $13,262m × 22.0% + (-$99m) = $2,818.64m. Pretax income = $2,818.64m - $790m net non-operating expense + $0m pretax adjustments = $2,028.64m. Net income attributable to Deere = $2,028.64m × (1 - 26.0%) + $0m = $1,501.19m. Diluted EPS = $1,501.19m / 270.0m × 1 = $5.56/share. Linked revenue equals the requested absolute Q2 worldwide net sales and revenues forecast of $13,262m.
assumptions: The 22.0% operating margin is a pre-discrete Q2 margin derived from guidance-based sales phasing and expected seasonal earnings concentration; the $99m settlement is separately recognized as a discrete Q2 SG&A/legal item.
The $790m net non-operating expense is a rounded Q2 interest/other non-operating estimate anchored to Q2 2025 interest expense and Q1 2026 lower borrowing-rate commentary.
The 26.0% tax rate is the midpoint of management's 25%-27% FY2026 guidance.
Diluted shares are 270.0m; this is consistent with Q1's 270.9m diluted shares after allowing for the announced ongoing repurchase program, without assuming an unannounced acceleration.

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Q2 2026 PPA operating-profit forecast = prior reported Q1 2026 actual $139m + GUIDANCE $490m + E6 (-$99m) = $530m. E1-E5, E7-E8 and COMPARABLES contribute $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA sales volume, price, currency, production cost, warranty and regional/product mix
event_contributions.transmission_path: FY PPA sales and margin guidance is phased to fiscal Q2 using Q2 2025 PPA seasonality. Guided double-digit quarterly margins for the balance of FY2026 support a Q2 margin above Q1's 4.4%, while the FY 11%-13% range and later-year geographic normalization constrain the estimate.
assumptions: FY2026 PPA sales use the midpoint of management's -5% to -10% range: -7.5%.
Q2 PPA revenue uses the FY2025 Q2 base rather than a simple quarterly pro rata.

Q2 operating margin is 13.0%, within the logic of double-digit quarterly margins after Q1 and slightly above the 12.0% FY midpoint because management expected geographic mix to normalize later in the year.
The FY reconciliation uses FY2026 midpoint PPA operating profit of $16,013m × 12.0% = $1,922m.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. FY2026 PPA sales midpoint = FY2025 $17,311m × (1 - 7.5%) = $16,013m. Q2 PPA sales = FY2025 Q2 $5,230m × 92.5% = $4,838m. Q2 pre-discrete PPA operating profit = $4,838m × 13.0% = $628.94m, rounded to $629m. FY reconciliation: FY midpoint PPA operating profit $1,922m less Q1 actual $139m less Q2 $629m leaves $1,154m for Q3-Q4 on $8,012m of remaining sales, or 14.4%, consistent with management's expectation for later-year mix normalization. Change versus Q1 actual = $629m - $139m = +$490m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA production cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: The import surcharge could increase PPA component and whole-good costs, reducing segment operating profit through cost of sales. Deere's guided tariff-cost outlook already captures the broad tariff environment.
assumptions: No incremental PPA-specific surcharge cost was disclosed beyond management's tariff estimate.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental PPA operating-profit effect = $0m because tariff exposure is embedded in the GUIDANCE margin range and no distinct Q2 PPA amount is available.

event_contributions.affected_line: Financing cash flow and equity
event_contributions.transmission_path: The dividend has no PPA operating-profit effect.
assumptions: No operational transmission is evidenced.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. PPA operating-profit effect = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA selling price, shipment volume and financing support
event_contributions.transmission_path: Farmer aid can support demand while calls for lower tractor prices can pressure realization. Deere's PPA outlook already includes government liquidity support, challenging farm fundamentals and positive price realization.
assumptions: No Deere-specific price, incentive, production or order-book change was disclosed.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental PPA operating-profit effect = $0m; mixed macro signals are already contemplated and cannot be converted defensibly to a segment-profit amount.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA sales volume and dealer inventory
event_contributions.transmission_path: Acreage intentions affect eventual farmer economics and equipment replacement, but do not establish an immediate Q2 PPA production or sales-volume change.
assumptions: No Deere-specific volume elasticity or Q2 shipment response is disclosed.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental PPA operating-profit effect = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA material and component cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: Section 232 changes could change PPA production costs, then gross margin and segment operating profit, but the extent of affected PPA imports and mitigation is not disclosed.
assumptions: Management's tariff-cost and price-cost guidance already includes tariff uncertainty.
No separate PPA Q2 cost amount is available.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental PPA operating-profit effect = $0m; avoid double counting guided tariff headwinds.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA selling, administrative and general expense / legal settlement accrual
event_contributions.transmission_path: The proposed class settlement concerns repairs of certain large-agriculture equipment. The central case assigns the stated fund to PPA legal/SG&A expense, reducing PPA operating profit directly without affecting PPA net sales.
assumptions: The full $99m announced settlement fund is assumed accrued in fiscal Q2.
The expense is assigned to PPA because the settlement covers certain large-agriculture-equipment repairs; no cross-segment allocation was disclosed.
No offsetting Q2 aftermarket revenue or insurance recovery is assumed.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Interpolate the unchanged PPA guidance first to $629m of Q2 pre-discrete operating profit, then recognize the full assumed Q2 settlement expense: $629m - $99m = $530m. Incremental PPA operating-profit effect = -$99m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA sales volume and Financial Services credit availability
event_contributions.transmission_path: Lower farm working capital could reduce replacement demand, but higher cash farm income partly offsets. Management already expected unfavorable row-crop economics and possible higher receivable write-offs.
assumptions: No Deere PPA order, production or margin revision was reported.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental PPA operating-profit effect = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Future PPA demand and mix
event_contributions.transmission_path: Higher projected crop prices can improve replacement economics, but the report was published after the fiscal Q2 end and offers no evidence of a recognized Q2 PPA sale or margin effect.

event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. PPA operating-profit effect = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA sales volume, price and production cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: CNH and AGCO indicate weak large-equipment retail and tariff/freight pressure, partly offset by pricing and precision demand. These drivers are already reflected in Deere's guided PPA sales decline and margin range.
assumptions: No peer-to-Deere PPA margin-transfer coefficient is defensible.
Peer company-specific factory utilization, geographic mix, accounting bases and share effects are excluded.
event_contributions.calculation: Incremental PPA operating-profit effect = $0m. The comparable summary's preliminary add-on is zero, and a quantitative peer transfer would double count guided PPA demand and tariff assumptions.
